titre: The Athens Charter Was Not Published in 1933, the Year It Is Named For
accroche: The text that invents modern urban zoning appears only eight years after the 1933 congress whose name it bears, and at first without its author's name.
contenu_vulgarise:
In July 1933, architects and urban planners board the liner S.S. Patris at Marseille for the fourth International Congress of Modern Architecture (CIAM). The round trip takes them to Athens on August 3; they sail back on August 10. The chosen theme is “the functional city”: separating housing, work, leisure, and circulation into distinct zones, rather than letting them tangle together as in the old city. The congress debates and votes on observations to that effect.

## A Text Left in the Drawer for Eight Years

What the congress produces on its return does not circulate. The text known today as the “Athens Charter” (the four functions, zoning, the preservation of old neighborhoods, 95 points in all) appears only in 1941, in the middle of the Occupation, in a small book published in Paris without an author's name, signed only by the “4th Congress.” The Canadian Centre for Architecture, which preserves this lineage in its catalog, notes it plainly: the principles adopted at Athens eight years earlier are indeed taken up there, but it is this 1941 publication, not the congress itself, that launches the text into public debate.

## A Signature That Waits Sixteen Years More

The author of this anonymous book is a mystery to no one in the profession: it is Le Corbusier, who so deeply reworked the congress's collective observations that the article devoted to them presents it as the expression of his personal ideas more than the result of a vote. Yet he signs the text with his name only in 1957, in a new edition from Éditions de Minuit preceded by an opening address by Jean Giraudoux: twenty-four years after the congress, and sixteen years after the first publication.

It is this signed version that is read, and that carries weight: it inspires postwar reconstruction, from the large housing estates of the Unité d'habitation in Marseille to the towers of Brasília, zoning cities according to the text's four functions. It will also be criticized as early as 1953 by a younger generation of CIAM, Team X, which reproaches it for its rigidity, before precipitating the movement's dissolution. The zoning it popularizes will later feed projects as disputed as the Pruitt-Igoe housing complex in St. Louis. The text that bears the name of a 1933 congress was therefore never voted as such by that congress: it took a single one of its participants to rewrite it, and nearly two more decades for him to claim it.

repere.texte: The text published in 1941 under the sole signature of the “4th Congress” is signed by Le Corbusier with his own name only in 1957, by Éditions de Minuit: twenty-four years after the 1933 Athens congress, and sixteen years after the first publication.
repere.source: Canadian Centre for Architecture (CCA), catalog record

carte.punch: The Athens Charter was not written by the 1933 congress that gives it its name.
carte.idee: The text known as the Athens Charter popularizes urban zoning in four functions. But the 1933 congress that inspires it never published it: it appears eight years later, anonymous, rewritten by Le Corbusier alone, who will sign it with his name only in 1957.

quiz.question: Why did the text voted by the 1933 CIAM congress not immediately influence postwar urban planning?
choix: Because the text was published, and largely rewritten by Le Corbusier, only eight years later, in 1941
Because the congress was canceled before reaching a final text
Because the four functions chosen (living, working, leisure, circulation) were judged unworkable
Because Le Corbusier refused to let the text be published before the end of his career
quiz.explication: The congress publishes nothing accessible in 1933; the text that bears its name appears only in 1941, under the sole signature of the “4th Congress” and heavily reworked by Le Corbusier, who will sign it with his name only in 1957. The congress was not canceled, the four functions did structure postwar urban planning, and nothing indicates a refusal to publish on Le Corbusier's part.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What are the four functions that the Athens Charter proposes to separate into distinct zones in the city?
choix: Living, working, relaxing, and getting around
Sleeping, eating, getting care, and learning
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The text holds four urban functions to be separated into zones: living, working, relaxing, and getting around; the other three lists do not match the text's nomenclature.

quiz_supplementaire.question: In what year does Le Corbusier first sign the Athens Charter with his own name?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Le Corbusier signs the text with his name only in 1957, in an edition from Éditions de Minuit preceded by an opening address by Jean Giraudoux; 1933 is the year of the congress, 1941 that of the first anonymous publication.
